title: Harness: render.html's Google Fonts URL fails for families without a 100..900 weight axis, so the re-render falls back to the default serif
evidence: gen-pseudo-decor: the blockquote in 'Playfair Display' renders as Times in render.png. `curl 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Playfair%20Display:ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900'` returns HTTP 400, because Playfair's wght axis is 400–900. Many popular AI choices are affected (Playfair Display, DM Serif, Bebas Neue, Pacifico, Lobster, static-only families), so the diffs blame the plugin for font differences Figma would not have.
rootCause: dev/render.html renderTree(): it always requests `family=X:ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900`, and onerror simply resolves.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this independently. In dev/render.html renderTree() (around line 220), every non-generic family is requested as `family=X:ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900`, and the result is ignored because of `l.onload = l.onerror = r`. I checked the URLs with curl:
- That URL returns HTTP 400 for Playfair Display, Bebas Neue, Pacifico and DM Serif Display.
- It returns 200 for Inter and Roboto, which have a full 100–900 weight axis.

In dev/out/gen-pseudo-decor.json the blockquote segment is {families:['Playfair Display','serif'], weight:400}. render.png clearly draws that blockquote in Times, so part of the case's diff blames the plugin for a font that Figma would render correctly.

This is a renderer artifact only. ui.html and code.js are not involved, and Figma ships these fonts.

The proposed fix is mostly right but needs one correction. Discrete instances are lenient only when at least one requested instance exists:
- `Playfair Display:wght@450` returns 200.
- `Bebas Neue:ital,wght@0,400;1,400` returns 200.
- `Pacifico:ital,wght@0,400;0,700` returns 200.
- `Bebas Neue:wght@450` and `Bebas Neue:wght@700` return 400, because no requested instance exists.

So the plain `family=X` fallback is required, not optional. Also, a `<link>` with onerror cannot retry by itself. The cleanest approach is to fetch() the CSS first (Google Fonts CSS sends CORS headers) and try URLs in order.

A side note on the original page, not part of this finding: it loads only Playfair wght@700, so Chrome uses the 700 face for weight 400 there. Figma would use Playfair Regular. A small residual diff on that blockquote would therefore remain even after the fix.

title: render.html Google Fonts request asks for wght 100..900 + ital on every family, which returns HTTP 400 for most families, so the render falls back to system fonts
evidence: `curl 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Plus%20Jakarta%20Sans:ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900'` returns 400. Playfair Display and JetBrains Mono also return 400. Only Inter (full 100..900 axis) returns 200. text-hero renders in Helvetica-like fallback instead of Plus Jakarta Sans / Playfair (diff 6.9% at 1440, 12.6% at 390, almost all of it font mismatch).
rootCause: dev/render.html renderTree(): `l.href = …family=${f}:ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900` assumes every family has a full weight axis and an italic.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this independently. dev/render.html, in renderTree at line 220, builds one stylesheet link per family with the URL `family=F:ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900`. I checked it with curl. Inter, Roboto and DM Sans return 200. Plus Jakarta Sans, Playfair Display, JetBrains Mono and Poppins return 400. Google rejects the whole request when the family's weight axis does not cover 100..900, when the family has no italic, or when it is a static family. When the request fails, the onerror handler resolves silently, so the render falls back to system fonts.

The existing outputs show this. dev/out/text-hero.render.png has the headline, body and stat numbers in a Helvetica-like fallback, and the quote in a Georgia-like bold italic. dev/out/text-hero.orig.png uses Plus Jakarta Sans and Playfair Display. Because the fallback font has different glyph widths, the headline wraps onto 2 lines instead of 3 and the vertical layout shifts. Most of the diff for any case that uses a non-Inter Google font comes from this harness bug, not from the plugin. That makes those cases' text-fidelity numbers unreliable, which is why I rated it high for the harness. Real Figma is not affected, since Figma ships every Google Font.

The proposed fix only partly works. Requesting exact tuples still returns 400 when a tuple names a weight or italic the family does not offer. For example, `Playfair Display:ital,wght@0,100` and `Poppins:wght@450` both returned 400, and one bad tuple sinks the whole request. Exact tuples are fine when they are valid: `Bebas Neue:ital,wght@0,400;1,400` and an unsorted `Playfair Display:ital,wght@0,700;0,400` both returned 200. The bare `family=F` fallback does work (200), but it only loads weight 400.

title: Renderer draws text with the CSS family list instead of the font code.js resolves, so font substitution is invisible to the harness
evidence: text-tw-pricing segments have family '-apple-system', which render.html passes through as a generic family → SF Pro, the same as the original. In Figma, code.js resolveFont gives Inter. Missing families ('Totally Missing Font') also render with the browser fallback, not with the GENERIC_FAMILIES choice. dev/mock-figma.js only lists Inter/Arial/Roboto Mono/Georgia, so resolution is not realistic either.
rootCause: dev/render.html build() uses s.font.families directly. mock-figma.js does not report the resolved fontName per segment.
fix:
These are harness-only changes. ui.html and code.js stay as they are.

1) dev/mock-figma.js, realistic font list
- Build FONTS from a committed dev/google-fonts.json. It is a list of {family, styles[]}, with real style names from Google Fonts metadata (e.g. "Regular", "Medium", "SemiBold", "Bold", "Italic"). Inter keeps Figma's "Semi Bold"/"Extra Bold" spelling.
- Do not include OS-only families (SF Pro, Helvetica, Helvetica Neue, Arial, Georgia, Times New Roman, Menlo, Segoe UI) by default. This models Figma in the browser and the worst case.
- Add an env flag, e.g. FIDELITY_LOCAL_FONTS=mac. It appends the macOS families to model desktop Figma with local fonts.
- Keep giving every listed style to loadFontAsync so existing cases keep loading.

2) dev/mock-figma.js, export the resolution code.js actually uses
- Keep the vm context object (const ctx = {...}; vm.runInNewContext(src, ctx)). Top-level function declarations in code.js become ctx properties.
- After the import finishes, call `const get = await ctx.prepareFonts(doc.root);`. This is the same closure code.js uses, including the fallback to FALLBACK_FONT on a failed load.
- Walk doc.root and, for every TEXT segment, set `s.figmaFont = get(s.font)` (a {family, style} object).
- Write the annotated doc back to the JSON path given on argv. Alternatively, print a marker line such as `FONTS_JSON:` followed by the JSON, which fidelity.mjs then parses.
- Do not rely on recording setRangeFontName. Mock TEXT nodes cannot be mapped back to tree segments without ids.

3) dev/fidelity.mjs
- It already runs the mock before rerender. After the mock, re-read OUT/<name>.json (or parse the FONTS_JSON line) and pass that annotated doc to rerender().
- If the mock crashes, fall back to the original doc.

4) dev/render.html
- When s.figmaFont is present, set `span.style.fontFamily = '"' + s.figmaFont.family + '"'` with no CSS fallback list.
- Set fontWeight and fontStyle from the resolved style name, using the same regex table as code.js describeStyle (thin=100 ... black=900, /italic|oblique/). Do not use s.font.weight, so a missing weight (Inter Regular standing in for 300) is visible.
- The font loader collects s.figmaFont.family instead of s.font.families, and loads Google CSS only for families that are not local-OS families.
- When figmaFont is absent, keep today's behavior.

Result: text-tw-pricing renders in Inter and text-hero's missing-font line in Noto Serif (or Georgia under FIDELITY_LOCAL_FONTS=mac). Any wrap or height change from font substitution then shows up in diffPct and heightDelta. Cases whose CSS already names a Google Font, such as text-hero's Plus Jakarta Sans and landing's Inter, are unaffected.
verifierNotes:
I checked this against the code and it holds up. dev/render.html build() sets span.style.fontFamily straight from s.font.families, which is the CSS stack. -apple-system and system-ui pass through unquoted as generic families, so Chrome draws SF Pro, the same font as the original screenshot. The font loader at around line 210 also only fetches Google Fonts for the CSS family names.

In fidelity.mjs the mock (execFileSync mock-figma.js) runs before rerender(doc), but rerender only gets the agent's doc. Whatever code.js resolves is thrown away. mock-figma.js also offers only Inter/Arial/Roboto Mono/Georgia.

Evidence from the cases:
- In dev/out/text-tw-pricing.json, 43 of 44 segments use the Tailwind default stack ('-apple-system,system-ui,Segoe UI,Roboto,...').
- text-hero has 'Totally Missing Font,Another Missing,Georgia,serif'.
- landing has a bare 'Arial'.

I loaded code.js in a vm with a Google-only font list (Inter, Roboto, Noto Serif, PT Serif, Arimo, ...) and called resolveFont:
- -apple-system resolves to Inter.
- 'Totally Missing Font..., Georgia, serif' resolves to Noto Serif.
- Arial and Helvetica resolve to Inter, because they are not in GENERIC_ALIASES.
- ui-monospace resolves to Inter (JetBrains Mono when it is in the list).

I re-ran node dev/fidelity.mjs text-tw-pricing and got diffPct 1.98. In the diff PNG the body text barely differs, because both sides use SF Pro. The red is the heading wrap and other non-font differences. So reflow from SF Pro or Georgia being swapped for Inter or Noto Serif in Figma never shows up in diffPct. That affects nearly every Tailwind or system-font page.

This is a harness problem, not a plugin bug. Severity is medium: it hides real metric drift such as line wraps and heights, but changes no output.

The proposed fix has the right direction but needs corrections:
- Mapping setRangeFontName calls on mock nodes back to tree segments needs node ids that the mock does not have. Calling code.js's own resolver per segment is simpler and exact.
- A realistic list should not drop OS fonts outright. Desktop Figma with local fonts does list SF Pro, Helvetica, Georgia and Arial. A Google-only default plus an opt-in flag is the honest model.

As a side note, the plugin itself maps Arial/Helvetica to Inter rather than to a metric-compatible Arimo, and Georgia to Noto Serif rather than to a closer serif. That would be a separate plugin finding.

title: mock-figma/render.html lack the text APIs needed by the fixes above
evidence: dev/mock-figma.js Text class has no textTruncation, maxLines, paragraphIndent, paragraphSpacing, listSpacing, setRangeListOptions, setRangeIndentation, setRangeTextDecorationStyle/Color/Thickness/Offset. Its textCase list rejects SMALL_CAPS / SMALL_CAPS_FORCED. render.html ignores TEXT effects (text-shadow), decoration style/color, truncation and indent.
rootCause: The mock and renderer only model the API subset code.js currently uses.
fix:
Only the harness files change (dev/mock-figma.js and dev/render.html). Nothing in ui.html or code.js changes.

**1. dev/mock-figma.js, Text class**

Node-level setters (each stores its value, so other code can read it back):
- `set textTruncation(v)`: `oneOf(v, ['DISABLED','ENDING'])`
- `set maxLines(v)`: if `v !== null`, call `num(v)` and fail when `v < 1` or `v` is not an integer. Do NOT fail when truncation is DISABLED (Figma allows it).
- `set paragraphSpacing(v)`, `set paragraphIndent(v)`, `set listSpacing(v)`: `num(v)`, and fail when `v < 0`
- `set textAlignVertical(v)`: `oneOf(v, ['TOP','CENTER','BOTTOM'])`
- `set textCase` and `set textDecoration` (node-level): same value lists as the range versions below

Range methods (each first calls `this._range(a, b)`):
- `setRangeTextCase`: allow `['ORIGINAL','UPPER','LOWER','TITLE','SMALL_CAPS','SMALL_CAPS_FORCED']`
- `setRangeTextDecorationStyle(a,b,v)`: `oneOf(v, ['SOLID','WAVY','DOTTED'])`
- `setRangeTextDecorationColor(a,b,v)`: `keysOnly(v, ['value'])`, then either `v.value === 'AUTO'` or `checkPaint(v.value)` with `v.value.type === 'SOLID'`
- `setRangeTextDecorationThickness(a,b,v)` and `setRangeTextDecorationOffset(a,b,v)`:
  - if `v.unit === 'AUTO'`: `keysOnly(v, ['unit'])`
  - otherwise: `keysOnly(v, ['value','unit'])`, `oneOf(v.unit, ['PIXELS','PERCENT'])`, `num(v.value)`
- `setRangeTextDecorationSkipInk(a,b,v)`: fail if `typeof v !== 'boolean'`
- `setRangeListOptions(a,b,v)`: `keysOnly(v, ['type'])`, `oneOf(v.type, ['ORDERED','UNORDERED','NONE'])`
- `setRangeIndentation(a,b,v)`: `num(v)`, and fail when `v < 0` or `v` is not an integer
- `setRangeParagraphSpacing(a,b,v)`, `setRangeParagraphIndent(a,b,v)`, `setRangeListSpacing(a,b,v)`: `num(v)`, and fail when `v < 0`
- `setRangeHyperlink(a,b,v)`: `v` is null, or `{type:'URL'|'NODE', value:string}`

Other mock fixes:
- `checkEffect`: add `'blurType'` to the BLUR allowed keys and check it with `oneOf(e.blurType, ['NORMAL','PROGRESSIVE'])` when present.
- `checkPaint` SOLID: also allow `'visible'` and `'blendMode'`.

**2. dev/render.html**

render.html draws the agent tree, so each new tree field is handled here at the same time as the code.js change that maps it to the Figma API. Suggested field names: `n.truncate` (bool), `n.maxLines`, `n.paragraphSpacing`, `n.paragraphIndent`, `s.decorationStyle`, `s.decorationColor`, `s.decorationThickness`, `s.decorationOffset`, `s.list` / `s.indent`.

In `build()`, inside the TEXT branch and before the early return:
- **Text shadow:** for `(n.effects || [])` where `type === 'DROP_SHADOW'`, push `` `${e.offset.x}px ${e.offset.y}px ${e.radius}px ${rgba(e.color)}` `` and set `el.style.textShadow` to the joined list. Leave out spread: CSS text-shadow has none, and Figma ignores spread on text. Also apply LAYER_BLUR as `filter`.
- **Truncation:**
  - if `n.truncate && n.maxLines`: `display:-webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; -webkit-line-clamp:n.maxLines; overflow:hidden`
  - else if `n.truncate` only: `overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis` with a fixed height
- **Paragraphs:** `text-indent` from `paragraphIndent`. Render paragraph spacing by splitting segments on `\n` into block children with `margin-bottom = paragraphSpacing`.
- **Decoration, per span:** set `textDecorationStyle` (`solid`/`wavy`/`dotted`), `textDecorationColor`, `textDecorationThickness` (px or %), and `textUnderlineOffset`.
- **Text case:** map SMALL_CAPS to `font-variant-caps: small-caps` and SMALL_CAPS_FORCED to `all-small-caps`.
- **Lists:** draw a bullet or number prefix and `padding-left` of `indent * listIndentStep`.
verifierNotes:
I checked this against the code. No case was cited, so I did not re-run the harness. Every factual claim holds.

What the mock lacks today:
- dev/mock-figma.js's Text class only has setRangeFontName, setRangeFontSize, setRangeFills, setRangeTextDecoration, setRangeLetterSpacing, setRangeLineHeight and setRangeTextCase, plus setters for textAutoResize and textAlignHorizontal.
- setRangeTextCase only accepts ORIGINAL, UPPER, LOWER and TITLE. It wrongly rejects SMALL_CAPS and SMALL_CAPS_FORCED, which are valid in the real API.
- Any fix that calls setRangeListOptions, setRangeIndentation, setRangeTextDecorationStyle/Color/Thickness/Offset or setRangeParagraphSpacing would hit a TypeError ("not a function") in the mock. That shows up as a MOCK CRASH, so the mock cannot validate those fixes.

What the renderer lacks today:
- In dev/render.html, build() returns early for TEXT before shadows(n.effects) runs. Text effects (text-shadow) are never drawn.
- Decoration only maps to underline or line-through. There is no decoration style or color, no truncation and no indent.

Two points in the proposal are imprecise:
1. The mock objects are plain class instances, so assigning a property with no setter (for example t.textTruncation = 'ENDINGX', t.paragraphSpacing = NaN, t.textAlignVertical) passes silently. Node-level properties are only checked if the mock adds explicit setters for them.
2. render.html draws the agent's JSON tree (fidelity.mjs rerender(doc) passes doc to renderTree), not the Figma nodes code.js builds. So "render them in render.html" really means "render the new tree fields that code.js will map to these APIs". The tree field names have to be defined at the same time as the plugin fixes, or the renderer has nothing to read.

The proposed maxLines rule ("maxLines only when truncation is ENDING") is stricter than real Figma. Figma accepts maxLines (a number of at least 1, or null) whatever textTruncation is set to; the value only has an effect when truncation is ENDING. Failing on it would flag valid code.

Related mismatches I found in the same files:
- checkEffect's keysOnly for BLUR rejects 'blurType', which newer API versions expect. code.js setEffects works around this with a try-and-fallback.
- The SOLID paint check rejects the valid keys 'visible' and 'blendMode'.

This is a real harness gap, not a plugin bug. On its own it changes nothing users see, so low severity is right. It is a prerequisite for checking the text-feature fixes.

title: render.html draws GRADIENT_ANGULAR as a radial gradient (not 'not drawn' as documented)
evidence: paint-effects render: the bg-conic tile and the 'from 180deg at 25% 50%' tile show concentric elliptical rings, and the donut chart becomes an orange ring on gray. In render.html paintLayer(), every non-LINEAR gradient goes into the radialGradient branch.
rootCause: dev/render.html paintLayer(): `else def = <radialGradient …>` handles GRADIENT_ANGULAR as well as GRADIENT_RADIAL.
verifierNotes:
The finding is correct. In dev/render.html, paintLayer() handles every /^GRADIENT_/ paint with `if (p.type === 'GRADIENT_LINEAR') … else def = <radialGradient …>`, so GRADIENT_ANGULAR (and GRADIENT_DIAMOND) are drawn as SVG radial gradients. The documentation says angular "isn't drawn", which is wrong.

I checked dev/out/paint-effects.render.png, which is newer than both render.html and ui.html, against orig.png:
- The bg-conic tile (row 5, col 3) renders as concentric elliptical red/yellow rings, but the original is a conic sweep.
- The tile with `from 180deg at 25% 50%` (row 5, col 4) renders as purple/blue ellipses centred in the middle.
- The donut, `conic-gradient(#6366f1 0 42%, …)`, renders as an orange ring on gray instead of indigo/green/orange/gray sectors.

The JSON confirms the plugin emits GRADIENT_ANGULAR there. So the diff pixels in those tiles come from the renderer, not only from the plugin.

It is still real, but I rate it low, not medium. It cannot affect users, it only matters for cases that use conic gradients, and the plugin also has its own conic bugs (below), so those tiles would differ anyway.

The proposed fix is roughly right but too loose:
1. A CSS conic-gradient on a w×h layer div is not stretched with the box. A Figma angular paint lives in normalised layer space, so its angles are distorted on non-square layers. The CSS version would not match that.
2. "angle+90" assumes Figma's identity angular gradient starts at 3 o'clock and runs clockwise. That is my understanding (Figma dev-mode CSS for a default angular is `conic-gradient(from 90deg at 50% 50%, …)`), but it should be checked against one real Figma export.

The cleanest emulation uses a canvas with the full affine transform (corrected fix below).

Separately, this exposes real plugin gaps in ui.html gradientPaint() that should be reported on their own:
- For conic gradients it drops `from <angle>` and `at <pos>` and always emits an identity transform.
- Because Figma's identity angular starts at 3 o'clock while CSS conic starts at 12 o'clock, even plain `conic-gradient(...)` donuts come out rotated 90° in real Figma.

Once the renderer is fixed, the harness will show these instead of hiding them behind radial rings.

title: render.html paints fills as child divs on top of the node's own inset box-shadow, hiding every INNER_SHADOW
evidence: paint-borders: the input with 'shadow-inner ring-1 ring-inset ring-slate-300' has INNER_SHADOW {spread:1} and INNER_SHADOW {y:2,blur:4} in the JSON, but the render shows no border line. The bg-slate-200 'pressed' tile with two inset shadows and the indigo inset 0 0 0 1px ring look flat. The glass card's inset highlight also disappears.
rootCause: dev/render.html build(): box-shadow (including inset) is set on the element, and fill layers are appended as absolutely positioned child .layer divs, which paint above the element's own inset shadow.
verifierNotes:
The gap is real, and it is in the renderer, not the plugin. In dev/render.html, build() calls shadows(n.effects), which puts both DROP_SHADOW and INNER_SHADOW into a single el.style.boxShadow. It then appends each fill as an absolutely positioned `.layer` child created by paintLayer(). CSS paints an element's inset box-shadow just above its own background, which is below its positioned descendants. So whenever a FRAME or RECT has both fills and an INNER_SHADOW, the fill layer covers the inner shadow completely.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs paint-borders` (diffPct 1.89) and checked the JSON. The plugin output is correct:
- The input has INNER_SHADOW {y:2, blur:4, a:.05} and INNER_SHADOW {spread:1, slate-300}, with a white fill.
- The indigo card has INNER_SHADOW {spread:1, indigo a:.25} plus 3 drop shadows.
- The bg-slate-200 tile has two INNER_SHADOWs.

In render.png none of these appear: the input has no border line, the card has no ring, and the tile is flat. All of them are visible in orig.png. In real Figma an inner shadow is drawn above the node's fills and below its children, so the plugin's output would look right there. The harness misrepresents it.

I checked the proposed fix on a scratchpad copy of the repo with a patched render.html. After the patch, the input border, the indigo ring and the pressed tile's inset shading all render, matching orig.png, and paint-borders diffPct drops from 1.89 to 1.85. Nothing else changed visibly. The fix is safe:
- Children are appended after the new layer, so they still paint above it, which matches Figma.
- The stroke overlay keeps z-index 1, so it stays on top.
- Nodes without inner shadows are unaffected.

The remaining diffs in this case (avatar ring, the Revenue card's left accent, Focused/outline rings, ellipse radii, per-side border colors) are separate plugin issues, not this one.

One small refinement: Figma lists effects bottom-to-top, but CSS treats the first box-shadow as topmost. The inset list should therefore be reversed before it is joined. This only matters when inner shadows overlap and are semi-transparent.

title: Effect order disagreement between plugin and renderer (ring/ring-offset stacks drawn in the wrong order)
evidence: paint-borders avatar 'ring-4 ring-white ring-offset-2 ring-offset-indigo-500': the JSON effects are [white spread 6, indigo spread 2] (parseShadows reverses the CSS order). render.html joins effects in array order into box-shadow (first = top), so the white ring covers the indigo offset, which the original shows. The 'Upgrade plan' button's white offset gap is missing for the same reason.
rootCause: ui.html parseShadows() `return out.reverse()` assumes Figma draws the last effect on top, like fills. dev/render.html shadows() assumes index 0 is on top. One of them misrepresents Figma.
fix:
1) Check the convention once in Figma. In the plugin console run: `const r=figma.createRectangle(); r.resize(100,100); r.effects=[{type:'DROP_SHADOW',color:{r:1,g:0,b:0,a:1},offset:{x:0,y:0},radius:0,spread:20,visible:true,blendMode:'NORMAL'},{type:'DROP_SHADOW',color:{r:0,g:0,b:1,a:1},offset:{x:0,y:0},radius:0,spread:5,visible:true,blendMode:'NORMAL'}];`. If you see a thin blue band inside a red one, the last effect is on top, as the plugin assumes. If you see only red, index 0 is on top.

2a) Expected outcome (last = top). Fix only the harness. In dev/render.html shadows(), keep the loop as it is and return `{ boxShadow: out.reverse().join(', '), filter, backdrop }`. CSS draws the first entry on top, so reversing turns Figma's last-on-top order into CSS order. Leave ui.html and code.js unchanged.

2b) Other outcome (index 0 = top). Fix the plugin. Remove `.reverse()` from ui.html parseShadows() so it returns `out`. CSS order then maps 1:1 to Figma order, and render.html stays as it is. Nothing in code.js changes, because setEffects() passes the array through unchanged.

3) Separate renderer fix, needed either way. INNER_SHADOW is drawn under the fill layers. In build(), take the inset entries out of el.style.boxShadow. After the fills loop, append one overlay `div.layer` (absolute, inset 0, border-radius inherit, pointer-events none) whose boxShadow lists only the inset shadows, in the same reversed order as step 2a. Do this when n.effects contains any INNER_SHADOW. Inner shadows then paint above the fills, as Figma draws them.

4) Add a comment at the end of parseShadows() and in render.html shadows() stating the convention, so the two cannot drift apart again.
verifierNotes:
The plugin and the renderer disagree about effect order, and I confirmed it in both the code and the pixels. ui.html parseShadows() (line 472) ends with `return out.reverse()`, so CSS box-shadow order (the first entry is drawn on top) becomes "last entry on top", the same convention Figma uses for fills. dev/render.html shadows() (lines 68-77) joins the effects in array order into one CSS box-shadow, which treats index 0 as the top layer.

Evidence from dev/out/paint-borders.json:
- Avatar (`ring-4 ring-white ring-offset-2 ring-offset-indigo-500`): effects are [DROP_SHADOW spread 6 white, DROP_SHADOW spread 2 indigo]. In the CSS, the 2px indigo offset is listed first, so it sits on top of the 6px white ring.
- "Upgrade plan" button: effects are [shadow-lg x2, ring 4 indigo-300, offset 2 white].

I cropped and enlarged the orig and render PNGs. The original avatar has a thin indigo ring inside a white ring. The render shows only white. The original button has a white 2px gap inside its indigo-300 ring. The render has no gap, just a solid light-indigo band. So the reported symptom is real and comes from this ordering mismatch.

What I could not settle from the repo is which side matches real Figma. Neither the code nor the mock documents the convention, and the Plugin API docs (as I remember them) do not state an effects draw order. The plugin's choice (last = top) matches Figma's fills convention and its newest-on-top panel lists, so the renderer is more likely the side that is wrong. That makes this a harness issue: it produces false diffs on every Tailwind ring-offset element, plus a few false passes. Severity is low, because shadows only cover each other visibly when opaque zero-blur rings overlap.

One caveat: if a check in Figma shows index 0 on top, the bug is in the plugin instead, and it would be medium severity. Tailwind's ring-offset is very common on focus states, avatars and buttons, and in Figma the offset gap would disappear.

The proposed fix (check once in Figma, then align one side) is the right procedure. I made it concrete below and added a related renderer defect I found while checking. render.html applies INNER_SHADOW as an inset box-shadow on the node's element, but the fills are separate absolutely positioned `.layer` child divs painted above that box-shadow. Inner shadows are therefore hidden under any fill. In paint-borders, the input's `ring-1 ring-inset` border and the gray `shadow-inner` pill both disappear in the render. Real Figma draws inner shadows above fills, so this is another harness artifact.

title: Mock/renderer reject or ignore the Figma paint features needed by the fixes (blendMode, image filters, TILE/CROP, masks)
evidence: dev/mock-figma.js checkPaint keysOnly allows only ['type','color','opacity'] / ['type','gradientTransform','gradientStops'] / ['type','imageHash','scaleMode']. It would flag valid Figma keys: paint.blendMode, paint.visible, ImagePaint.filters/scalingFactor/imageTransform/rotation. The mock has no createEllipse/isMask/maskType. render.html draws IMAGE TILE/CROP as cover and ignores node/paint blendMode.
rootCause: dev/mock-figma.js checkPaint/Node and dev/render.html paintLayer() model only the subset code.js emits today.
fix: Harness-only change; the plugin is unaffected. In dev/mock-figma.js: (1) Define a shared list of blend modes, BLEND = ['PASS_THROUGH','NORMAL','DARKEN','MULTIPLY','LINEAR_BURN','COLOR_BURN','LIGHTEN','SCREEN','LINEAR_DODGE','COLOR_DODGE','OVERLAY','SOFT_LIGHT','HARD_LIGHT','DIFFERENCE','EXCLUSION','HUE','SATURATION','COLOR','LUMINOSITY']. (2) In checkPaint, add 'visible', 'opacity' and 'blendMode' to the allowed keys of every paint type, gradients included (they already have opacity in real Figma). Check them with `if (p.blendMode !== undefined) oneOf(p.blendMode, BLEND.filter(b => b !== 'PASS_THROUGH'), 'paint.blendMode')`, a boolean check for visible, and num() with a 0..1 range for opacity. (3) For IMAGE, also allow 'scalingFactor' (number > 0), 'rotation' (a multiple of 90), 'imageTransform' (a 2x3 numeric matrix, valid only when scaleMode === 'CROP') and 'filters'. filters may only contain the keys exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint, highlights and shadows, each a number in [-1, 1]. (4) On the node base class, add real setters so these values are validated, not silently stored: blendMode (oneOf BLEND), isMask (boolean), maskType (oneOf ['ALPHA','VECTOR','LUMINANCE']) and rotation (num). (5) Add createEllipse(), which returns a Rect-like shape node with type 'ELLIPSE' and an optional arcData setter ({startingAngle, endingAngle, innerRadius} as numbers), appended to the page the same way createRectangle is. In dev/render.html: (a) For IMAGE with TILE, set backgroundRepeat to 'repeat' and backgroundSize to `${naturalW*(p.scalingFactor||1)}px ${naturalH*(p.scalingFactor||1)}px`. The natural size comes from loading the image first. (b) For CROP, invert imageTransform the same way the gradients already do (inv = invert(t)), then set backgroundSize to (inv[0][0]*100)% (inv[1][1]*100)% and backgroundPosition to pixel offsets of -t[0][2]*inv[0][0]*W and -t[1][2]*inv[1][1]*H. Alternatively, draw an with a CSS transform equal to the inverse matrix scaled to the layer's W and H. (c) Map paint.blendMode to mix-blend-mode on that paint's layer div, so it blends with the paint layers below it inside the node's isolated stacking context. Map node.blendMode (other than PASS_THROUGH or NORMAL) to mix-blend-mode on the node element. PASS_THROUGH means no isolation, NORMAL on a frame means isolation:isolate. Convert the names to lower-case with hyphens; LINEAR_BURN and LINEAR_DODGE have no CSS equivalent and fall back to color-burn and color-dodge. (d) When a child has isMask, wrap that child and all the siblings after it in one container. Give that container a CSS mask-image made from the mask node's rasterized shape: alpha for ALPHA and VECTOR, mask-mode luminance for LUMINANCE. (e) Draw ELLIPSE nodes as a div with border-radius:50%. Keep all of these changes additive so the existing cases still produce the same diffs.
verifierNotes:
I checked this against the source and it holds. In dev/mock-figma.js, checkPaint uses keysOnly with exact allow-lists: SOLID allows ['type','color','opacity'], gradients allow ['type','gradientTransform','gradientStops'], and IMAGE allows ['type','imageHash','scaleMode']. Any valid Figma paint key outside those lists makes the mock fail. That covers visible and blendMode on any paint, opacity on gradients (which the finding missed), and filters, scalingFactor, imageTransform and rotation on IMAGE. The figma object only has createFrame, createRectangle, createText, createNodeFromSvg, createImage and createImageAsync, so calling createEllipse would throw a TypeError.

One part of the finding is overstated. The node class only defines setters for some properties, so node.blendMode, node.isMask, node.maskType and node.rotation are not rejected. They are stored as plain properties and never validated, and the renderer ignores them.

In dev/render.html, paintLayer handles IMAGE as `backgroundSize = scaleMode==='FIT' ? 'contain' : 'cover'`. TILE and CROP are therefore drawn as cover, and no blend mode is ever applied. Today this does not affect any output: ui.html only emits FILL and FIT (FIT_MODES = {contain, scale-down}), code.js passes scaleMode through and only sets node.opacity, and no current case uses these features. So nothing is broken now. The problem is that fixes proposed in other findings, such as background-repeat → TILE, mix-blend-mode → blendMode, or an elliptical border-radius → ellipse, would either fail validation in the mock or be drawn wrong by the renderer. That would make correct plugin changes look like regressions. The API surface in the proposal is accurate for real Figma: every Paint has visible, opacity and blendMode; ImagePaint has scaleMode, imageHash, imageTransform, scalingFactor, rotation and filters; nodes have isMask, maskType ALPHA|VECTOR|LUMINANCE and blendMode; and figma.createEllipse exists. A mask in Figma clips the siblings that come after it in the same parent, which matches the proposed renderer behaviour.

title: Harness is flaky on network: Tailwind CDN or picsum missing in one of the two renders produces huge bogus diffs
evidence: First run of paint-effects: the runner extraction had no Tailwind applied (tree with 24 layers, heightDelta 1572, everything stacked full-width), while the original screenshot had Tailwind but its picsum images broken. The rerun was clean (13.87%). paint-borders timed out ('timeout waiting for window.__result') on the first run and passed on the second. In paint-hero-bg the original fell back from Inter to Helvetica (Google Fonts link), while the render used Inter.
rootCause: dev/fidelity.mjs original() and extract() load remote assets independently with no retry or verification. Parallel agents share bandwidth.
fix:
These changes are all in dev/fidelity.mjs. The plugin needs no changes.

1) Deterministic local cache for remote assets (Tailwind, Google Fonts CSS and woff2, picsum/unsplash):
   - Right after the websocket opens, call send('Fetch.enable', {patterns:[{urlPattern:'*cdn.jsdelivr.net*',requestStage:'Request'},{urlPattern:'*fonts.googleapis.com*'},{urlPattern:'*fonts.gstatic.com*'},{urlPattern:'*picsum.photos*'},{urlPattern:'*fastly.picsum.photos*'},{urlPattern:'*images.unsplash.com*'}]}) on the BROWSER session (no sessionId). This also covers the sandboxed srcdoc iframe even when it runs out of process.
     Fallback: on each page session call s('Target.setAutoAttach',{autoAttach:true,waitForDebuggerOnStart:true,flatten:true}). Enable Fetch/Network on every child session from Target.attachedToTarget, then call Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger.
   - On each Fetch.requestPaused, hash the URL to dev/cache/<sha1>.bin plus a .meta.json holding status and headers. On a cache hit, call Fetch.fulfillRequest with {requestId, responseCode, responseHeaders including Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*, body: base64}.
   - On a miss, fetch the URL in Node with up to 3 tries and a 20 s timeout each, following redirects (picsum redirects to fastly.picsum.photos). Store the final body under the ORIGINAL URL, then fulfill.
   - Picsum URLs without a seed return a random image per request. Caching by URL makes the original and the extraction see the same bytes, which by itself removes one source of diff.
   - If the fetch still fails, call Fetch.continueRequest and record the URL in a per-case netErrors list.

2) Make failures visible: call Network.enable on both sessions (and child sessions). Push to the case's netErrors on Network.loadingFailed (not canceled) and on Network.responseReceived with status >= 400.
   In original(), also return:
   - brokenImgs: [...document.images].filter(i=>i.complete&&!i.naturalWidth).length
   - twOk: needsTw ? [...document.styleSheets].some(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules].some(r=>/--tw-|tailwindcss/.test(r.cssText))}catch(e){return false}}) : true
   - fontsFailed: [...document.fonts].filter(f=>f.status==='error').length

3) Retry: wrap the Promise.all([original(c), extract(c)]) step in a loop of up to 2 attempts. Retry when any of these holds: netErrors.length, brokenImgs, !twOk, fontsFailed, doc.images.some(i=>!i.bytes), or extract threw a timeout.
   If the last attempt still fails a check, keep the row but add a 'flaky' column listing the reasons, e.g. 'tw', 'img:3', 'net:fonts.gstatic.com'. That way nobody reads a bogus diffPct as a plugin regression.
   Also lower waitFor's timeout for extract to about 60 s and treat a timeout as retryable.
verifierNotes: I checked this against the code in dev/fidelity.mjs and dev/runner.html. I did not re-run the harness, because the failures are intermittent and one passing run would prove nothing either way. The code shows the claimed weakness is real. - original() and extract() run in parallel in two separate Chrome targets. Each one loads Tailwind (TAILWIND_CDN = https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tailwindcss/browser@4), Google Fonts and picsum/unsplash images from the network on its own. Nothing is shared or cached between them. - original() waits for document.fonts.ready, scrolls, and waits until every image is complete. But img.onerror also resolves that wait, so a broken image is screenshotted as if it were fine. A failed Tailwind

title: render.html: a frame's stroke overlay (z-index:1) escapes the node and paints over later siblings
evidence: layout-mobile-app@390: in render.png the .list frame's rounded bottom border is drawn on top of the fixed tab bar, and the tab bar's top border is drawn across the FAB '+' button. Neither happens in orig.png, and Figma would not do it either: the tree order is list, tabbar, fab.
rootCause: dev/render.html build(): the stroke div gets style.zIndex = 1, but the .n nodes (position absolute or relative, z-index auto) don't form stacking contexts, so the overlay joins an ancestor stacking context above later siblings.
fix: In dev/render.html build(): remove `s.style.zIndex = 1;` and stop appending the stroke overlay before the children. Keep a reference to it (`el._stroke = s;` instead of `el.appendChild(s)` inside `if (n.stroke) {...}`). Append it after the children loop: `for (const c of n.children || []) build(c, self, images); if (el._stroke) el.appendChild(el._stroke);`. The overlay is still absolutely positioned with `inset:0` and `border-radius:inherit`, so it is out of flex flow and clipped as before. Because it is the last positioned child with z-index auto, it paints above the frame's own fills and children, matching Figma's stroke-over-content order. It no longer paints above the frame's later siblings. This creates no new stacking contexts, so backdrop-filter and future blend-mode behavior are unchanged. (Alternative: `.n { isolation: isolate }` also fixes it, but makes every node a stacking context, which is unnecessary.) No changes are needed in ui.html or code.js.
verifierNotes:
Confirmed. I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs layout-mobile-app -w 390` (diffPct 0.3). The tree order under div.app is div.list (y 470–885, has a stroke), then nav.tabbar (y 824–900, stroke), then a.fab (y 800–860, no stroke). In the render PNG, the list's side borders and rounded bottom corner are drawn over the tab bar, and the tab bar's top border cuts across the FAB '+' button. orig.png shows neither. Figma would not show them either, because a frame's stroke belongs to that layer and is painted before the sibling layers that come after it.

Root cause is in dev/render.html build(). The stroke overlay div is `.layer` (position absolute) with `s.style.zIndex = 1`. The `.n` nodes are position absolute or relative with z-index auto, and most have no opacity, filter or other property that creates a stacking context. So the z-index:1 overlay is lifted into the nearest ancestor stacking context, which is usually the root, and paints above every later sibling with z-index auto. This is only a renderer artifact. ui.html and code.js are not involved, and the Figma output is unaffected.

The proposed fix (`.n { isolation: isolate }` or z-index:0 on every .n) would work, but it turns every node into a stacking context. That has side effects for backdrop-filter, and for any future blend-mode or pass-through emulation, since Figma frames default to PASS_THROUGH. A smaller fix needs no stacking contexts at all: drop the z-index and append the stroke overlay after the children. Then normal tree-order painting puts the stroke above the frame's own children, as Figma does, and below later siblings.

I checked this on a scratch copy of the repo (render.html patched there only, nothing in the project edited). The re-render no longer shows the list border over the tab bar or the line through the FAB, and diffPct went from 0.30 to 0.28.

title: Harness can't validate the Figma APIs needed for the layout fixes, and remote assets load independently on each side
evidence: dev/mock-figma.js Frame/Node have no layoutWrap, counterAxisSpacing, counterAxisAlignContent, layoutGrow, layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical, constraints, rotation/relativeTransform, numberOfFixedChildren, overflowDirection, itemReverseZIndex, strokesIncludedInLayout, maxWidth, or textTruncation/maxLines. A plain assignment would silently pass instead of being validated. layoutMode only allows NONE, HORIZONTAL and VERTICAL. render.html ignores wrap, grow and rotation. Separately, layout-legacy-structures.orig.png rendered in Arial (the Google Fonts request failed) and layout-mobile-app@390.orig.png has broken picsum avatars while the render shows them, which inflates diffPct for reasons unrelated to the plugin.
rootCause: The mock and renderer cover only the API surface code.js uses today. fidelity.mjs original() and extract() fetch the network separately, with no cache and no check of load status.
fix:
Edit only the harness files. These are dev/mock-figma.js, dev/render.html and dev/fidelity.mjs, which are maintained outside this verifier's no-edit scope.

1) dev/mock-figma.js: validate the new APIs and catch unknown properties.

1a) Strict but correct property checking:
- Build an ALLOWED set per node type. It must include every property code.js sets today, so the current cases keep passing: name, clipsContent, cornerRadius, fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing, textAutoResize and the other existing ones. It also includes the real Figma properties that may be adopted.
- Wrap each created node in `new Proxy(node, {set(t,k,v){ if(!ALLOWED[t.type].has(k) && !(k in t)) fail('unknown prop '+k); t[k]=v; return true; }})`.
- Internal `_` fields must bypass the check. Either test `k[0]==='_'` or assign them through the target.

1b) Validated setters:
- layoutWrap: oneOf NO_WRAP or WRAP. WRAP is only allowed when this.layoutMode === 'HORIZONTAL'.
- counterAxisSpacing: a number >= 0, or null.
- counterAxisAlignContent: oneOf AUTO or SPACE_BETWEEN.
- layoutGrow: must be 0 or 1. Fail if the parent is not Auto Layout.
- layoutSizingHorizontal and layoutSizingVertical:
  - Accept FIXED, HUG or FILL.
  - FILL fails unless the node is already appended to a parent whose layoutMode is not NONE.
  - HUG fails unless the node is a TEXT node or a frame whose own layoutMode is not NONE.
  - This catches the most common real error: setting sizing before appendChild.
- constraints: an object with exactly horizontal and vertical. Each is one of MIN, MAX, CENTER, STRETCH or SCALE.
- rotation: must be a finite number.
- minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight: a number >= 0, or null.
- itemReverseZIndex and strokesIncludedInLayout: booleans.
- Text nodes:
  - textTruncation: oneOf DISABLED or ENDING.
  - maxLines: an integer >= 1, or null. Fail if textTruncation is not ENDING.
  - paragraphSpacing: a number >= 0.
- Add GRID to layoutMode only when code.js starts emitting it.

2) dev/render.html:
- When building flex for a layout object:
  - wrap === 'WRAP' sets flex-wrap:wrap and row-gap to counterAxisSpacing. A HORIZONTAL frame's counter axis is the vertical one.
  - grow === 1 on a child sets flex:1 1 0 along the parent's main axis.
  - truncate on text sets overflow:hidden, text-overflow:ellipsis and -webkit-line-clamp to maxLines.
- rotation: Figma rotates counter-clockwise about the node's top-left. Draw it as transform:rotate(-<deg>deg) with transform-origin 0 0, keeping x and y as the rotated node's origin.

3) dev/fidelity.mjs original(): detect asset failures instead of caching.
- After the existing waits, also evaluate:
  - `[...document.images].filter(i=>i.currentSrc && i.naturalWidth===0).length`
  - `[...document.fonts].filter(f=>f.status==='error').length`
- Also check `document.fonts.check('16px "<family>"')` for each family named in the page's Google Fonts link.
- Print a netErr column, and warn when it is nonzero so diffPct isn't trusted for that run.
- In extract(), do the same check on the runner iframe, using the agent's image-fetch results.
- Optional: enable Fetch.enable with a URL-keyed cache in dev/out/.netcache, shared by both pages, for deterministic re-runs.
verifierNotes:
This is a harness gap, not a plugin bug. Part of it is confirmed and part could not be reproduced.

Confirmed in dev/mock-figma.js:
- Node and Frame are plain JS classes with setters only for the properties code.js uses today.
- An assignment to any other property quietly creates an own property and is never checked. So a typo like `layoutWrap = 'WRAPS'`, or `layoutSizingHorizontal = 'FILL'` on a child of a non-Auto-Layout parent, would pass the mock but throw in real Figma.
- Frame.layoutMode only accepts NONE, HORIZONTAL and VERTICAL.
- code.js uses none of layoutWrap, layoutGrow, layoutSizing*, rotation, constraints or textTruncation today (grep finds nothing). So this does not hide any current bug. It only matters once the layout fixes proposed elsewhere start using these APIs. That is why the severity is low.

render.html does turn Auto Layout into flex (line 12 says so, and `parent.layout.mode` is handled at lines 94-110 and 176-194). It has no handling for wrap, grow or rotation, so the renderer part of the fix makes sense.

Not reproduced: the asset-flakiness claim. In the current dev/out files:
- layout-legacy-structures.orig.png renders in Inter, not Arial, and all picsum images load.
- layout-mobile-app@390.orig.png shows all avatars loaded, matching the render.

The failure the reporter saw was a transient network failure. Still, the mechanism is real. In fidelity.mjs, original() and extract() each fetch over the network on their own. original() waits on document.fonts.ready and on image onload/onerror but never checks whether anything actually loaded. So an occasional network failure will inflate diffPct without any warning.

Problems with the proposed fix:
(1) A Proxy that rejects every unknown property would break the run right away. code.js already sets properties the mock has no setters for (name, clipsContent, cornerRadius, fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing and others). It needs an explicit allowlist of real Figma properties, not "anything without a setter".
(2) numberOfFixedChildren is a prototyping/scroll property, not part of Auto Layout. Validating it adds nothing.
(3) layoutMode GRID (gridRowCount/gridColumnCount) is a recent API. Add it only if code.js actually adopts it.
(4) An on-disk Fetch cache is optional. The cheaper, sufficient change is to detect failed loads and flag them.

title: The harness diffPct badly under-reports missing content
evidence: robust-react-cdn: every task card is missing (skeleton instead of 7 cards), yet diffPct is 0.83. robust-localstorage: the list, date and week grid are missing, yet diffPct is 1.29. For comparison, small text-kerning differences in other cases score 2–7%. Light content on a light background mostly stays under the per-channel threshold of 48. A large missing region is weighted the same as scattered anti-aliasing noise.
rootCause: dev/fidelity.mjs diff(): a global per-pixel max-channel threshold (>48) is averaged over the whole page. There is no structural or region signal.
fix:
Edit dev/fidelity.mjs only. The plugin is not touched.

1. Tile metric in diff(): while looping over pixels, also add the per-pixel mean absolute RGB difference into tile buckets of 16x16:
   `tile[(y>>4)*TW + (x>>4)] += (|dr|+|dg|+|db|)/3`
   After the loop, a tile is "bad" when tileSum/(tilePixelCount) > 6.
   - Report `tilePct = badTiles/totalTiles*100`.
   - Also report `contentTilePct = badTiles / tilesWhereEitherImageIsNotBackground * 100`. A tile counts as content when any pixel in it differs from the image's corner/background color by more than 8 in either image. This removes the dilution from empty page area.
   - In the diff PNG, tint bad tiles orange underneath the red per-pixel marks, so a missing card shows up as a block.
   - Keep the existing diffPct so old numbers stay comparable.

2. Text coverage:
   - In original(), extend the evaluated async function so it returns `text: (document.body.innerText||'').replace(/\s+/g,'')` alongside the height. innerText already skips display:none and visibility:hidden.
   - Pass it through `{png, h, text}`.
   - After extract(), compute `treeText` by walking doc.root and concatenating `seg.text` for every TEXT node's `segments`, with whitespace stripped. Do the same for input or placeholder values if the tree stores them there.
   - Report `textCov = min(1, treeText.length / max(1, origText.length))`.
   - For a more robust signal, also compute the multiset overlap of words (split on whitespace) between innerText and the joined tree text: `matchedWords/origWords`.
   - Flag the row (e.g. `textCov<0.9`) in the console table, the same way mockErrors are flagged.
   - Compare characters to characters, never words to characters.

3. Drop the DOM-element-count check, because legitimate layer flattening and expansion make it noisy. If a structural signal is wanted, compare the count of original elements with a non-transparent background or border that are larger than 24x24 against tree FRAME/RECT nodes with fills or strokes, and treat it as informational only.
verifierNotes:
Confirmed by re-running both cases. robust-react-cdn scored diffPct 0.68 and robust-localstorage scored 1.29. In robust-react-cdn.render.png all 7 task cards (badges, titles, due dates) and the column counts are replaced by three grey skeleton blocks per column. Yet robust-react-cdn.diff.png marks only the glyph pixels red. The white card bodies against the #e5e7eb skeleton blocks differ by about 26 per channel, which is under the >48 threshold in dev/fidelity.mjs diff(), so whole missing or extra boxes are not counted. robust-localstorage.diff.png has the same problem: the date, list rows, week grid and input are all shifted or missing, but the score is about 1%.

Two things water the metric down:
- The per-pixel max-channel threshold of 48 ignores low-contrast changes such as light surfaces on light backgrounds, which is the norm in Tailwind and shadcn-style UIs.
- `bad` is divided by W*H of the whole screenshot (1440x900+). Pages that are mostly empty background therefore push the score toward 0, so one missing card counts about the same as anti-aliasing noise.

This is purely a scoring problem in the harness. The missing content itself, where the agent captures the React or localStorage pre-hydration state, is a separate plugin-side issue and is not part of this finding.

The proposed fix is mostly right but has flaws:
- (2) compares a word count against a character count.
- (2) gives no way to get the original's text, because original() and extract() run in different pages and original() returns only the PNG and height.
- (3), the DOM element count against layer count, is too noisy to be useful, since wrappers are legitimately collapsed and pseudo-elements and SVGs are expanded. It would cause false alarms.

I could not check the "2-7% for kerning cases" comparison because summary.json is overwritten on each run. It does not change the conclusion.

title: The harness can hang, or fail differently from the plugin, on slow or large assets, and renders with the OS colour scheme
evidence: (a) dev/runner.html awaits frame.onload with no timeout, while ui.html proceeds after 20 s. The first runs of robust-dashboard and robust-mobile-shell failed with 'timeout waiting for window.__result' because of slow image downloads, where the plugin would have continued. (b) With a 21 MB result (one 4200px photo), `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-dashboard` hung for more than 7 minutes with no output. waitFor() polls `window.__result` with returnByValue, transferring the full string every 250 ms over CDP. (c) Headless Chrome follows the macOS dark mode, so robust-mobile-shell rendered its dark theme. Results then depend on the machine.
rootCause: dev/runner.html (no load timeout), dev/fidelity.mjs waitFor/extract (polls the whole payload), and newPage (no emulated media).
fix:
These changes are for the harness owner. They touch only dev/runner.html and dev/fidelity.mjs.

1) dev/runner.html: make the load wait behave like ui.html.
`await new Promise((r) => { const t = setTimeout(r, 20000); frame.onload = () => { clearTimeout(t); r(); }; frame.srcdoc = html + ...; });`
Also put a 90 s timeout on the message wait, as ui.html does, and set `window.__result = JSON.stringify({error: ...})` when it fires.

2) fidelity.mjs: make a dead socket and a stuck call fail instead of hanging.
- Add `ws.addEventListener('close', () => { for (const p of pending.values()) p.reject(new Error('CDP socket closed')); pending.clear(); })`.
- Give send() a timeout, for example 120 s. When it fires, delete the id from `pending` and reject.
- Wrap each case in a try/catch, together with an overall per-case timeout, for example `Promise.race([runCase(f), sleep(180000).then(() => { throw new Error('case timeout'); })])`. Then one bad case is reported in the table and the run moves on.

3) fidelity.mjs: never pull more than about 2 MB through a single CDP response. Tests show the socket dies on incoming messages of 5 MB or more.
- extract(): first `await waitFor(p, 'typeof window.__result === "string" ? window.__result.length : 0')` to get the length. Then fetch the string in pieces: `for (let i = 0; i < len; i += 2e6) parts.push(await p.eval('window.__result.slice(' + i + ',' + (i + 2e6) + ')'))`, and `JSON.parse(parts.join(''))`. The payload is ASCII JSON with base64, so 2e6 characters stays well under the limit.
- shot(): when the image could be large, either capture in vertical tiles of about 2000 px using `clip.y` and stitch them in the diff page, or capture with `Page.captureScreenshot` and `format: 'png'` only after checking `w*h`. Otherwise use `IO.read`-style chunking: write the PNG to a page-side variable and slice it in the same way.
- Apply the same slicing to any diff() eval that returns base64.
- Optional: in runner.html, downscale image bytes larger than about 4 MB before storing them in `__result`, since the plugin would embed them anyway.

4) original(): put a 20 s timeout on the image wait to match the plugin: `await Promise.race([Promise.all(...), new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20000))])`.

5) newPage(): pin the colour scheme so results do not depend on the machine.
`await s('Emulation.setEmulatedMedia', { features: [{ name: 'prefers-color-scheme', value: process.env.H2F_SCHEME || 'light' }] })`
Apply it to all four pages (original, runner, render, diff), and optionally expose it as a `--dark` flag.
verifierNotes:
This is a harness-only problem. ui.html and code.js are not involved. I checked each of the three claims separately.

(a) Confirmed from the code. dev/runner.html line 28 waits for the iframe load with `await new Promise(r => { frame.onload = r; frame.srcdoc = ... })` and has no timeout. ui.html (around lines 1287-1290) gives up waiting after 20 s (`setTimeout(resolve, 20000)`) and continues anyway. extract() polls through waitFor() with a 90 s cap. So a page whose images take longer than about 90 s fails in the harness with 'timeout waiting for window.__result', while the plugin would carry on after 20 s. original() in fidelity.mjs has the same problem: inside a Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise it waits on `Promise.all(images.map(onload/onerror))` with no timeout, so a stalled image can block it forever.

(b) The symptom is real, but the reported mechanism is wrong. waitFor() does not transfer the payload every 250 ms. While `window.__result` is undefined, each poll returns almost nothing, and the first truthy evaluation returns the value once, which ends the loop. I tested the real cause with a standalone script. It launches Chrome headless=new the same way fidelity.mjs does and talks to it over Node 24's built-in WebSocket:
- Sending from Node to Chrome works up to at least 30 MB (a 30 MB expression evaluated in about 0.5 s).
- Receiving from Chrome works at 4 MB (Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue).
- At 5 MB or more, the CDP WebSocket closes immediately with code 1006.

fidelity.mjs has no 'close' handler on the socket, and send() has no timeout. Once the socket dies, every pending promise stays unresolved forever. waitFor's 90 s limit cannot fire either, because it is stuck awaiting page.eval. That fits the reported run: a 21 MB result hung for more than 7 minutes with no output. The same limit applies to page.shot() (Page.captureScreenshot returns base64), so a tall 1440 px page full of photos whose PNG exceeds about 4 MB would also hang. So would anything in diff() that returns base64 PNGs through eval.

(c) Confirmed. `defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle` returns Dark on this Mac. dev/out/robust-mobile-shell@390.orig.png renders the case's @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) theme, and the extracted root fill in the JSON is #0e0e1a. The original and the agent run in the same Chrome, so the diff stays self-consistent. Results still depend on the machine, and nothing in fidelity.mjs pins the colour scheme.

Note: the plugin's own iframe inside Figma desktop probably also follows the OS or app theme. That is a possible product question, but it is not part of this harness finding.

title: The harness can't show image-paint fixes or oklch-in-SVG: render.html draws every IMAGE as centred cover/contain, renders SVG in Chrome, and mock-figma rejects new ImagePaint keys
evidence: render.html paintLayer(): backgroundSize = FIT ? contain : cover, position center. CROP/TILE/imageTransform/scalingFactor/filters are ignored. mock-figma.js checkPaint IMAGE: keysOnly(['type','imageHash','scaleMode']), so filters/imageTransform/scalingFactor would be flagged as errors. render.html injects the SVG into Chrome, which understands oklch(), so the Tailwind-v4 SVG colour bug shows a 0% diff.
rootCause: dev/render.html paintLayer / build(SVG), dev/mock-figma.js checkPaint and createNodeFromSvg.
fix:
Harness-only changes. The plugin bug that this gap hides is fixed separately in ui.html svgNode.

A) dev/mock-figma.js checkPaint IMAGE:
keysOnly(p, ['type','imageHash','scaleMode','opacity','visible','blendMode','rotation','imageTransform','scalingFactor','filters'], 'IMAGE').
- oneOf scaleMode in FILL/FIT/CROP/TILE.
- If opacity is set: num in [0,1].
- If rotation is set: one of 0, 90, 180, 270.
- If imageTransform is set: require scaleMode === 'CROP' and a 2x3 array of finite numbers.
- If scalingFactor is set: require scaleMode === 'TILE' and a finite number > 0.
- If filters is set: keysOnly(filters, ['exposure','contrast','saturation','temperature','tint','highlights','shadows']), each a number in [-1,1].

B) dev/mock-figma.js createNodeFromSvg(svg), after the '<svg' check:
- For every match of /\b(fill|stroke|stop-color|flood-color|lighting-color|color)="([^"]*)"/g, accept the value only if it matches /^(none|currentColor|transparent|#[0-9a-f]{3,8}|rgba?\([^)]*\)|[a-z]+|url\(#[^)]+\))$/i and does not match /^(oklch|oklab|lab|lch|hwb|color|hsla?)\(/i. Otherwise fail('svg color not parseable by Figma: ' + value).
- Collect the ids with /\sid="([^"]+)"/g. For every href="#x", xlink:href="#x" or url(#x) whose x is not among them, fail('svg dangling reference #' + x).
These become mockErrors, so the media-tw-icons regression appears in the table.

C) dev/render.html paintLayer IMAGE. Preload the image (new Image(); await decode) to get nw and nh, then use the layer size W×H:
- FILL: cover, center, no-repeat (as now).
- FIT: contain, center, no-repeat (as now).
- TILE: background-repeat: repeat; background-size: (nw*(p.scalingFactor||1))px (nh*(p.scalingFactor||1))px; background-position: 0 0.
- CROP with imageTransform [[a,b,tx],[c,d,ty]] (it maps layer-normalised space to image-normalised space; this sketch ignores b and c, which only matter for rotation): background-size: (W/a)px (H/d)px; background-position: (-tx/a*W)px (-ty/d*H)px; no-repeat. CROP without imageTransform falls back to FILL behaviour.
- rotation: rotate an inner div that carries the background by that many degrees, swapping width and height for 90 and 270.
- filters (approximate, so do not use it to tune numbers): CSS filter = brightness(2^exposure) contrast(1+contrast) saturate(1+saturation), applied to that paint-layer div only.
- opacity: set the div's opacity.

D) dev/render.html build(SVG): before el.innerHTML = n.svg, run the same colour check as in B. For any unsupported colour attribute, put a red 2px outline on the SVG box (or swap the value for '#000') so the problem appears in the diff PNG and does not render correctly. Add the same treatment for dangling #id references.
verifierNotes:
I checked each claim against the code.

1) dev/render.html paintLayer(): every IMAGE paint gets backgroundSize = FIT ? 'contain' : 'cover', backgroundPosition 'center' and no-repeat. CROP, TILE, imageTransform, scalingFactor and filters are never read. Confirmed.

2) dev/mock-figma.js checkPaint: IMAGE runs keysOnly(p, ['type','imageHash','scaleMode']). That list also leaves out other valid ImagePaint keys (opacity, visible, blendMode, rotation, imageTransform, scalingFactor, filters), so any future fix that sets them would show up as a false mockError. Confirmed. The mock's createNodeFromSvg only regex-checks '<svg' and reads width/height. It never inspects colours or references. Confirmed.

3) oklch in SVG: ui.html svgNode() copies getComputedStyle values for SHAPE_PROPS and STOP_PROPS straight into attributes. In Chrome, computed values for Tailwind v4 colours stay in oklch(). The existing output dev/out/media-tw-icons.json holds 8 such values, e.g. fill="oklch(0.596 0.145 163.225)" and stroke="oklch(0.666 0.179 58.318)". The same appears in gen-tw-controls, layout-grid-stacking, layout-zorder-transforms, paint-effects and paint-mobile-cards. render.html puts n.svg into Chrome with innerHTML, and Chrome reads oklch correctly, so the diff cannot show the problem. code.js passes the same string to figma.createNodeFromSvg, and Figma's SVG importer is not known to read CSS Color 4 functions. So this is a real blind spot hiding a likely real plugin bug: icons wrongly coloured, probably black or missing. That bug should be filed separately as kind "plugin". Its root cause is ui.html svgNode, and the fix is to run every colour value through the existing parseColor() (canvas normalisation) and write it out as #rrggbb plus a separate fill-opacity/stroke-opacity/stop-opacity.

Context for the image part: code.js toPaint() currently sends only {type, imageHash, scaleMode}, and FILL in Figma is centred cover. So the renderer is accurate for what the plugin outputs today. The gap blocks checking future image fixes (object-position, background-position/size/repeat) and is not causing false diffs now. That makes it a real harness gap at medium severity.

Corrections to the proposed fix:
- The CROP mapping must use pixel offsets, not percentages.
- TILE needs the image's natural size, which means preloading the image.
- The mock must also accept opacity, visible, blendMode and rotation.
- The colour check should accept hex, rgb()/rgba(), named colours, none, currentColor and url(#id). It should flag oklch, oklab, lab, lch, color() and hwb. hsl() is better flagged too, since Figma support is uncertain and the plugin can always normalise.
- The <use>/url(#id) check is valid. svgNode clones only the <svg> element, so sprite references (<use href="#icon">) to a <symbol> elsewhere on the page arrive in Figma empty.

title: Harness timing and network flakiness: 90 s waitFor timeout with many remote images, and the orig screenshot can show failed or mid-animation media
evidence: The first version of media-images (24 remote images, ~2-8 s each from this machine, load average ~20) hit 'timeout waiting for window.__result' 3 times. The agent alone needed 29-96 s. In media-tw-icons the orig screenshot shows broken-image icons for picsum images that the agent loaded fine, which inflates diffPct to 33%. media-embeds orig shows Chart.js bars mid-animation.
rootCause: dev/fidelity.mjs waitFor(..., 90000), and original() and extract() fetch the network independently in parallel. original() only waits 400 ms after scroll for JS animations.
verifierNotes:
I checked dev/fidelity.mjs and re-ran the case. The problem is real and it is in the harness, not the plugin.

Code:
- waitFor(page, expr, ms = 90000) has a hard-coded 90 s limit.
- The main loop runs `Promise.all([original(c), extract(c)])`, so the screenshot page and the agent page fetch the same remote assets at the same moment. Both pages use one Chrome --user-data-dir, so the HTTP cache is already shared. But because they run in parallel, neither page gets a warm cache, and both compete for bandwidth.
- original() only waits for `document.images` that are not yet `complete` (onload/onerror). It never waits for CSS background-image URLs or video posters. It does not check naturalWidth, so a failed image counts as done.
- KILL_MOTION only stops CSS animations. JS/rAF animation such as Chart.js keeps running. After the load event the page waits only about 500 ms, then scrolls, then waits 400 ms.

Evidence:
- Before my run, the stored media-embeds.orig.png had no hero photo and no `.corner` or `.natural` background images. The agent tree reported 7 images with 0 missing, and diffPct was 28.42.
- I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs media-embeds` with no code changes. It took 2 min 36 s for this one case. diffPct dropped to 10.87, and imagesMissing went from 0 to 2: this time the network failed on the agent side.
- In the new orig.png the hero photo is only partly decoded or blurry, and both corner background images are still missing.
- The new orig.png also caught the Chart.js bar chart mid-animation: all bars squeezed into the "Jan" slot. In the earlier run the chart had finished.
- So the same code gives an 18-point diffPct swing, plus false red areas that could lead other verifiers to blame the plugin.

The current media-tw-icons.orig.png looks fine, so I could not reproduce the broken-image icons there. That fits a network race that happens only sometimes.

Changes to the proposed fix:
- "Share one Chrome profile" is already done, so it adds nothing. What helps is running the two steps one after the other.
- Waiting on document.images alone would not have caught the main failure seen here, which was CSS background images. The wait must cover those too.

Severity is low because users see no effect. It only makes the fidelity numbers and diff PNGs untrustworthy for cases with many images or JS animation.
